searchText: I've proposed a new beacon API endpoint for getting blinded blocks (ones that already exist): https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/241 Feedback on implementation complexity + willingness please 😁 (for Lighthouse the impl is straight-forward) looks good. Hi all, I'm attempting to understand what an event of `chain_reorg` with `depth: 0` means. Would this mean that there were no common ancestors? where did you see this? the definitions of re-org depth are pretty client specific so it may be a quirk of that client teku, self hosted node cc <@680234424037670912> then 😉 Do you have the message you're referring to? depth appears on the eventStream, can't find it in the normal reorg message, which appears to just list roots and slot numbers... if you can find the reorg from the BN it will give the slot of common anscestor, and the new / previous head slot and root... depth is `new head slot - common anscestor slot` in the places i've been searching... potentially the actual 'Reorg event' message on BN would be clearer to see what happened... ``` { slot: '4683774', depth: '0', old_head_block: '0xb942665c2eb6093ce53e46db6f458fbd32f5ec44f320ad63b569854592cbd26e', new_head_block: '0xeed75ccb5201c46614121324c7203e23b22ca166741fdb59bb426482b76369c4', old_head_state: '0x5b3363a7d5d7e2d38400742402e0b7b9be2fe8ce57c814aa7c035b983a715570', new_head_state: '0xe73d572c268d568284c919bb4e25951d27dc0bca48ce6e99ccde3db386ea8603', epoch: '146367', execution_optimistic: false } ``` After double checking, I'm not completely sure if when running i was using Infura API or My node Thanks for the event, really appreciate it. I think it's fair to say that a reorg length 0 is 'odd', so i've raised a ticket on teku and we'll have to figure out exactly how it occurred - can track via https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/issues/6197 if curious. I'd probably ignore them as a user, but from our side it's curious and we'll figure it out.
